data.name: Tabatha

paths.asana: Tabatha instance task in the sys-atlas project

data.summary: Tabatha is a cross-platform attention operating system — one product across five surfaces sharing a single Supabase spine. Reality is far ahead of every document that describes it: the workspace portfolio claims 'extension v4.x shipped, desktop v0.1.0, mobile in progress', but git HEAD is extension 6.7.82 (614 commits, 364 of them in July 2026 alone), the desktop companion is a shipped Tauri app at 0.3.10, and there is a Wear OS watch at 0.2.2 that no portfolio doc mentions at all. The mobile story is the biggest correction: BOTH standalone mobile repos are dead — tabatha-mobile (Expo, 19 commits, all May 2026) and tabatha-mobile-2 (native Android, 6 commits, all on one day, 2026-05-30, and it is now a Google AI Studio design lab in the `com.example` package, not a shipping app). The live phone surface is Tabby Sidecar, an Expo app living INSIDE the main repo at `sidecar/`, deployed as a PWA to tabatha.pondocean.co/sidecar. Distribution is the real bottleneck: two self-hosted channels (staff GitHub-release channel and an enterprise CRX force-install line) are both live at 6.7.78, four versions behind HEAD, while the Chrome Web Store item exists as a DRAFT that has never been published — the listing doc still reads 'NOT submitted' and the publishing credentials were never provisioned on this machine. Flux is not a sibling: Tabatha's entire backend IS the Supabase project literally named 'Flux' (ref mtdgoahskcibjbhfvofx), and Tabatha's tracker home is the 'Flux Development' Asana project, not the near-empty 'Tabatha Development' one. The wounds are concentrated and known: ~23 unescaped innerHTML sinks across gatekeeper.js and inbar.js that are cross-user reachable today via manager RLS scoping, an RLS gap letting a revoked device un-revoke itself, and two named sync arbitration root causes (A: recency-based arbitration; D: clock adoption duplicating shifts) that have a plan number reserved (047) and nothing built. The engineering machine itself is unusually strong — 40 live worktrees, 63 unit-test files, a version-sync pre-commit gate, a daily automated Asana status survey — which is exactly why the docs drift: the code moves faster than anything written about it.

nodes.label: Gatekeeper
nodes.activity: 7/25: 6.7.76 closed the [object Object] sanitize gap on gatekeeper's own intentHistory/intentPresets read — self-healing repair-on-read now writes corrected data back.
nodes.blurb: The intentional-friction layer and Tabatha's founding idea: before you can consume a page you must declare why you are there. Contrary to the portfolio's description it is NOT the new-tab override (that is home.html) — it is an all-URLs content script at document_start that intercepts navigation to any page, rendering a closed shadow-DOM gate. Complete and heavily hardened: a synchronous dim placeholder goes up before any await so the page cannot render underneath the gate, and a 2500ms timeout tears it down rather than trapping the user.
nodes.deep:
Files: src/content/gatekeeper.js (679 lines, single IIFE, closed shadow DOM). Decision logic lives in src/background/services/tabService.js checkContextNeeded() at ~L473.

States: (1) double-injection guard on #tabatha-gatekeeper-host; (2) fast local pre-check of settings.gatekeeperEnabled — a missing or unreadable setting FAILS TOWARD GATING; (3) indeterminate — synchronous dim placeholder with pointerEvents none so clicks still pass through; (4) CHECK_CONTEXT_NEEDED round-trip under withTimeout 2500ms; (5) confirmed — backdrop 0.85 strict / 0.6 relaxed, backdropFilter blur per settings.inpopBlurStrength, body overflow hidden in strict mode.

Bypass rules: chrome:// and chrome-extension:// URLs; a tab whose contextSource is already 'user' or 'url_rule'; Asana task URLs auto-derive context from page title (contextSource 'asana_auto', stores asanaTaskGid); a URL matching a parkedTabs entry restores its context and consumes the park; domains in skippedDomains.

web.label: Gatekeeper frame on the live /show showcase

nodes.label: Friction Exits
nodes.activity: 7/21: extension UX audit flagged the 8+-choice wall as contradicting the product's own Progressive Simplicity principle — promoted to an OVERHAUL theme, not a bug.
nodes.blurb: The seven distinct ways out of the gate, each a different classification of the impulse rather than a yes/no block. Continue, Side Quest (5 min timeboxed), Sugar Box (stash the craving, close the tab), Park, Later, Nevermind (close, logged as a focus win), and Dismiss (relaxed mode only) — plus a per-domain skip. Every exit emits LOG_INTENT_ACTION, so the friction layer is also the primary data source for the intent model.

nodes.label: Context Inheritance
nodes.activity: 7/24: cross-surface elapsed-drift fix (6.7.71) corrected the _startedAt back-dating that every other surface reads to compute elapsed time.
nodes.blurb: The Context Engine the concept doc promises: tabs inherit context from the parent intent declaration, and context propagates through browsing chains so a session can be reconstructed later. Active focuses are offered as inheritable presets in the gate (capped by settings.inheritItemCount). This is what turns declared intent into a running attention model rather than a one-shot prompt.

nodes.label: BlockGate
nodes.activity: 7/21: audit found its first sendMessage has no try/catch — an invalidated extension context throws unhandled and the block silently FAILS OPEN. One-line fix, still open.
nodes.blurb: The harder sibling of the Gatekeeper: a separate blocked-domain overlay that demands a 50+ character intent and a timer before it will let you through. Unlike the Gatekeeper it fails CLOSED on messaging failure by design. Backed by blockgateService.js, which also owns temporary unblocks and the Sugar Box stash.

nodes.label: InBar
nodes.activity: 7/25: B09 root-caused and specced — focus-list click sends only SWITCH_FOCUS and never saves the typed name. Not yet fixed.
nodes.blurb: The persistent in-page intent bar (1685 lines, the largest content script) — pause, sticky-note, inline notes, and voice-announced timer/drift overlays on every page. It is the only surface carrying the Backburner button that the spec promised on three surfaces. Partial because it hosts seven distinct auto-triggered overlays with no cooldown between them and no Escape-to-dismiss anywhere, and because B09 is open.

asana.label: 🐛 [bug] Pauses resumes everything that happens should be in the timeline log

nodes.label: URL Rules & Domain Intelligence
nodes.activity: Plan 038 shipped — domain history store drives auto-context so known domains skip the gate.
nodes.blurb: A rules engine that assigns context to URLs automatically, letting known domains bypass the gate with contextSource 'url_rule'. This is the pressure valve that keeps intentional friction from becoming intentional misery, and it is the substrate the smart-categorization roadmap item builds on.

nodes.label: Agent-vs-Human Gate
nodes.activity: 7/20: intake #218/#219 merged to staging — agent browsing detection and agent-vs-human history specced; the gate's 🤖 toggle exists, the history split does not.
nodes.blurb: A segmented control in the gate declaring whether a human or an agent is driving, firing START_AGENT_SESSION scoped to the tab. The toggle and session spans (C11a) are built; separating agent from human browsing in history and analytics is specced (#218/#219) but unbuilt. Matters more than it sounds — Malkio's own agents browse constantly, and unlabelled agent traffic poisons the attention data.

nodes.label: InPop Intent Dropdown
nodes.activity: 7/21: audit confirmed #212 unbuilt despite the InBar plumbing it would reuse already existing.
nodes.blurb: Feature #212 — an intent dropdown header for the intent popup. Confirmed unbuilt by the 2026-07-21 parity audit, which noted the reusable InBar plumbing is already there. Small, cheap, and still sitting in the backlog.

nodes.label: 23 Unescaped HTML Sinks
nodes.activity: 7/21: Koda's synthesis re-verified and found it WORSE than reported — ~23 sinks not ~12, and cross-user reachable TODAY, not contingent on a future feature.
nodes.blurb: No escapeHtml() helper exists anywhere in src/. About 23 distinct unescaped innerHTML sites across gatekeeper.js (4) and inbar.js (~19), including notes rendered raw inside a textarea and nine auto-triggered overlay sites. The exploitability was re-classified upward: focus_items.label already syncs to Supabase and is already readable cross-user through the manager/team RLS scoping in migration 012, so a malicious label set on one device renders unescaped in a manager's browser. This is the single highest-ranked NOW item in the audit and it is still open.

nodes.label: Gate Render Race
nodes.activity: Fixed — gatekeeper.js now attaches a synchronous dim placeholder before any await, so the page cannot paint under the gate.
nodes.blurb: The page could render before the intent gate appeared, because the overlay was built only after awaiting CHECK_CONTEXT_NEEDED plus two storage round-trips. Undermined the core 'declare intent before browsing' guarantee. Resolved by the synchronous placeholder pattern now visible in the code.

nodes.label: [object Object] Corruption
nodes.activity: 7/25: 6.7.76 closed the last hole — gatekeeper's own storage keys now sanitize and self-heal on read. 11 new unit tests.
nodes.blurb: Corrupted intentHistory and intentPresets rendered as literal '[object Object]' in a live gate, and crashed two React panels outright with 'Objects are not valid as a React child'. Fixed with a self-healing repair-on-read contract across gatekeeper.js and two sibling React read sites. A full sweep of every other direct storage read found no further sites in this corruption class.

nodes.label: GOAL: Friction That Survives Contact
nodes.activity: 7/21: the audit's OVERHAUL theme 7 (content-script modal discipline) is the current shape of this goal — 7 overlays, no cooldown, no Escape, an 8-choice wall.
nodes.blurb: The product bet: deliberate friction between impulse and action is a feature, not a bug — but only if users keep it switched on. The open work is discipline, not capability: seven auto-triggered overlays with no cooldown, no Escape-to-dismiss anywhere, and a gate offering 8+ choices that contradicts the project's own Progressive Simplicity principle.

nodes.label: Focus Engine
nodes.activity: 7/24: 6.7.73 hardened buildFocusRows against a malformed timestamp that could black out an entire install's sync cycle.
nodes.blurb: The 1798-line heart of the product — focus lifecycle, funnel transitions, and intent-to-focus linking. Every surface (extension, sidecar, watch, companion) is ultimately a view onto this engine's state. Its blast radius is the widest in the system: a throw inside its row-builder silently aborts the whole sync cycle, which is exactly the regression 6.7.73 fixed.

nodes.label: Focus Lifecycle
nodes.activity: Start / pause / resume / resolve / +5m extend, with funnel stages Unsorted → Todo → Focus → Addressing → Roadblocked → Resolved. Timer freezes on pause and rebases on resume, identically on all four surfaces.
nodes.blurb: The verbs of the system, and the one thing implemented consistently everywhere — the watch's TimerEngine is a pure Kotlin port that deliberately mirrors the Sidecar's focus.ts freeze-on-pause / rebase-on-resume math. Reaching that consistency took the 6.7.71 and 6.7.73 elapsed-drift fixes.

nodes.label: Checkpoint Progress Notes
nodes.activity: Live on extension, sidecar and watch. Five canned progress levels; staleness dot after 30 minutes; a checkpoint added on the wrist appears everywhere within a second.
nodes.blurb: Structured mid-focus check-ins — a note plus one of five progress levels (None / Little / A lot / Almost / Stuck). This is the highest-value capture moment in the product and the clearest proof that cross-surface sync works, since it round-trips watch → cloud → browser in about a second.

nodes.label: Backburner
nodes.activity: 7/25: B1 promoted — the spec promises the button on InBar, Home and Sidebar; only InBar ever got it. Backend is already generic; this is UI wiring only.
nodes.blurb: Send a focus to the back burner and pull it back later with resume / snooze / dismiss. Feature #207's own spec says it is 'Available on InBar, Homepage, and Sidebar' — two of the three surfaces never got the button. The message (BACKBURNER_FOCUS) and the data layer are already generic, so the gap is purely presentational.

asana.label: Backburner ANY focus from extension home/sidebar queue rows (UI wiring only — backend already generic)

nodes.label: Focus Queue & Priority
nodes.activity: 7/25: fuzzy search across all queue items from the new-intent box requested for both sidebar and sidecar — not built.
nodes.blurb: The ranked list of what is not being worked on right now, with P1–P5 priority selection and switch-to / resolve actions. Present on extension sidebar, home, and sidecar. Migration 021 added focus item priority server-side so the ordering survives across devices.

asana.label: Fuzzy search of ALL queue items from the new-intent box (sidebar + sidecar)

nodes.label: Sub-Intents
nodes.activity: Shipped to the Sidecar in v0.1.0 alongside checkpoints and backburner; nested queue rendering exists on the extension sidebar.
nodes.blurb: Nested focuses — break a focus into children that carry their own timers and appear in a nested queue. Data-layer complete and Sidecar-native; the parity audit flags that the extension renders them but does not offer the full CRUD the Sidecar does.

nodes.label: Clock & Work Shifts
nodes.activity: 7/25: #221 confirms there is NO way to fix a missed clock-in — clockIn()/clockOut() take no arguments and hardcode new Date().
nodes.blurb: Clock in / out / break with stint tracking, concurrent-shift guards, and abandoned-stint reconciliation across devices — the layer that turns attention data into billable hours. Partial for a blunt reason: the times cannot be edited. Work Shifts' 'Edit Shift' is a disabled stub, no EDIT_SHIFT handler exists, and the handlers ignore any payload passed to them.

nodes.label: Work Shifts Page
nodes.activity: Five controls ship as disabled buttons wearing a 'SOON' badge: Edit Shift, Delete, Export Week, Export PDF Timesheet, Sync to Cloud.
nodes.blurb: A dedicated page for shifts, schedules and the Live Stints panel that reconciles ghost sessions across installs. Honest about its gaps — five of its actions are explicitly badged as stubs rather than pretending to work, which is the pattern the one genuinely dishonest control (Break Notes) fails to follow.

nodes.label: Activity & Backdating Editor
nodes.activity: Drag/split/merge of time blocks, custom activity logs, and the retroactive-revision approval flow all carry 'Coming soon' copy.
nodes.blurb: The retroactive time-editing surface — where a day's tracked blocks get corrected after the fact. The viewer works; the editing verbs that make it useful (drag, split, merge) are unbuilt, which is why #221 treats clock recovery as an unsolved problem rather than a UI wiring job.

nodes.label: Unified Timeline
nodes.activity: 7/21: H7 — the timeline early-returns empty whenever sessions.length === 0, so anyone without the optional desktop companion sees a blank Context Activity with no explanation.
nodes.blurb: The single chronological view folding browser context, OS window sessions, and clock markers into one strip. It is the payoff for running every surface — and it is also the clearest example of the companion being treated as mandatory in code while being optional in product: users without it lose even their own clock markers.

nodes.label: Auto-Focus & Drift Detection
nodes.activity: Plan 036 shipped (v6.3.3–6.3.6); drift state now drives voice-announced overlays and push notifications.
nodes.blurb: Detects when attention has drifted from the declared focus and when a new focus should be inferred automatically. Drift is the signal that feeds the nudge system, the InBar amber state, and the drifted push notification — making it the connective tissue between passive tracking and active intervention.

gh.label: PR #21 — Intelligent Focus Lifecycle + Time Editing + URL Rules Domain Store (v6.3.3)

nodes.label: Off-Computer Toggle
nodes.activity: 7/19: parity audit calls its absence from the desktop companion an 'ironic gap' — the companion is the authority on whether you are at the computer, and cannot say so.
nodes.blurb: Marks a focus as continuing away from the machine so idle detection stops penalising it. Live on the extension sidebar and the Sidecar. The companion — which literally owns the idle and window signal that should drive it — has no such toggle, and the audit ranks adding it as the single highest-value companion addition.

nodes.label: Break Notes Never Persist
nodes.activity: 7/21: promoted as 'the one place in the whole audit where the UI actively lies about whether input was saved'.
nodes.blurb: BreakNotes saves to local React state only — the code comment literally reads 'In production this would persist via sendMessage.' Unlike its correctly-badged 'SOON' siblings it presents as a working input. Cheapest possible fix is the same stub badge used elsewhere; the real fix is a save handler into clockService.

nodes.label: B09 — InBar Edit/Assign Inconsistency
nodes.activity: 7/25: root-caused and specced in the 6.7.79 intake batch, with fix shape and acceptance criteria. Not yet implemented.
nodes.blurb: Clicking a focus in the InBar edit dropdown sends only SWITCH_FOCUS and never saves the name the user typed; pressing Save instead triggers autoQueueFromIntent, which severs the link just made and spawns a stray queued sub-focus. Two paths, two different wrong outcomes, on the surface users touch most often.

gh.label: PR #38 — docs(intake): 2026-07-25 batch — #220 agent session aggregation, B09 InBar root cause, parity/sync/voice audits (6.7.79)

nodes.label: Missed Clock-In Is Unfixable
nodes.activity: 7/25: #221 spec confirms no EDIT_SHIFT handler exists at all, and warns that editing times would insert a DUPLICATE row because shift sync IDs are hashed from the clock times.
nodes.blurb: Forget to clock in and the hours are simply gone — clockIn()/clockOut() hardcode new Date() and ignore any payload. Worse, the naive fix is booby-trapped: shift-row sync IDs are hashed from the clock times, so editing a time creates a duplicate row rather than updating one (this is sync Root Cause D). An immutable session id has to land first.

nodes.label: #221 Clock Backdate & Recovery
nodes.activity: 7/25: specced in 6.7.80 — backdated clock-in, real shift editing, and an evidence-ranked start-time proposal presented as confirm-or-adjust.
nodes.blurb: The spec that fixes the missed clock-in hole. Its cleverest part is the evidence ladder for proposing when you actually started: companion OS activity → first focus → capture frame → tab activity → calendar, offered as a confirmation rather than a guess. Also carries the consent model that Org Hours depends on.

nodes.label: Cross-Surface Elapsed Drift
nodes.activity: Fixed in 6.7.71 by back-dating _startedAt to mirror the Sidecar's resume math; 6.7.73 then hardened the same code against a malformed timestamp.
nodes.blurb: An active focus's elapsed time was undercounted by exactly its accumulated pause time on every surface but the extension, worsening with each pause/resume cycle — a concrete slice of Malkio's 'syncing between surfaces still a little off'. Fixed, with a red-to-green unit test, and then immediately re-hardened when adversarial review found the fix could throw.

nodes.label: MV3 Service Worker
nodes.activity: Reduced from a monolith to a 337-line entry by Plan 023; a single alarm router and a single auth owner now sit behind it.
nodes.blurb: The extension's spine. Everything the content scripts, pages and companion bridge do routes through this worker. Its known operational hazard is documented in CLAUDE.md as a hard rule: a stale worker running against swapped assets makes every sendMessage hang, which has already been root-caused as the cause of an apparent whole-product outage.

nodes.label: 37 Background Services
nodes.activity: Output of Plan 023's decomposition (PRs #1–#12, May 2026) — the monolith became 37 named services with a router skeleton.
nodes.blurb: The decomposed service layer: focus, sync, clock, tab, companion, capture, awareness, device, calendar, cortex and 27 more. This refactor is why the July velocity was possible — 364 commits in one month across 40 worktrees only works because the zones are separable. Plan 023 is the highest-leverage engineering decision in the repo's history.

nodes.label: Home / New Tab
nodes.activity: 7/21: header layout fix shipped (clock spacing, greeting cutoff, icon bunching, pill overlap).
nodes.blurb: The actual new-tab override (home.html) and the product's dashboard — FlipClock, Context Activity timeline, intents, initiatives, projects/clients, analytics and the activity heatmap in 2481 lines. Note this is what the manifest overrides; the Gatekeeper is a separate all-URLs intercept, a distinction every portfolio doc gets wrong.

asana.label: Home header layout fix: clock spacing, greeting cutoff, icon bunching, pill overlap

nodes.label: Sidebar (Side Panel)
nodes.activity: 7/19: parity audit made this the reference surface — 20 of its options are missing from the desktop companion.
nodes.blurb: The always-accessible command centre: five panels (focus, tasks, tabs, groups, stash) reachable on Ctrl+Shift+S. It is the de-facto specification of what a complete Tabatha surface looks like — every parity audit measures the companion, sidecar and watch against it.

nodes.label: Popup / Quick Switch
nodes.activity: 7/21: B9 — the search placeholder advertises Ctrl+Space while the real shortcut is Ctrl+Shift+E. One-line fix, open.
nodes.blurb: The toolbar popup for fast intent switching and tab search. Small and functional, but it tells users the wrong keyboard shortcut — a trivially fixable trust leak on the fastest path into the product.

nodes.label: Settings
nodes.activity: 7/24: 6.7.72 added the Asana PAT connect card, reaching parity with the Sidecar's Epic 3 integration.
nodes.blurb: 24 sections with search, live preview, and the panels for devices, org/team activity, Cortex, Asana and URL rules. Partial because 11 of the 24 live-preview panes render blank with no fallback message, and the information architecture is an explicit OVERHAUL theme — Cortex is buried under 'Privacy & Capture' and Team Activity sits at a different altitude from Devices.

nodes.label: Settings Live Preview
nodes.activity: 7/21: 11 of 24 sections render a blank preview pane with no fallback message. The cheap half (add the existing generic fallback string) is a NOW item.
nodes.blurb: A preview pane that shows what a setting will actually do before you commit to it — a genuinely good idea, half-delivered. Building real mockups for Context View and Blocked Sites is overhaul-scoped, but simply printing the existing fallback string everywhere it is missing is a same-day fix.

nodes.label: In-App Feedback → Asana
nodes.activity: 7/23: feedback-review agent protocol doc opened as TR-15; the pipeline itself is proven by live QA probes landing as Asana tasks.
nodes.blurb: A feedback widget that files bugs and ideas straight into the Asana intake board via an edge function, with a graceful fallback to a prefilled GitHub issue when unconfigured. Genuinely closed-loop: several tasks in the tracker are visibly the output of this widget, including QA probes.

asana.label: TR-15 feedback-review agent protocol doc

nodes.label: Hotkey Coverage
nodes.activity: Two commands registered in the manifest (Ctrl+Shift+S side panel, Ctrl+Shift+E tab list). #215 asks for comprehensive coverage; unbuilt.
nodes.blurb: Rapid intent declaration without touching the mouse — named in the roadmap's original feature backlog and still only two shortcuts deep. For a product whose whole thesis is reducing the cost of declaring intent, this is a conspicuously thin surface.

nodes.label: #222 Notes System
nodes.activity: 7/27: specced in 6.7.81 and filed to the tracker. Status check found there is no free-standing note anywhere in the product today.
nodes.blurb: A real notepad — a flat stream rather than a filing hierarchy, deliberately avoiding a second taxonomy competing with Contexts. The design answer to 'may or may not be connected to the current focus' is two fields: an immutable contextStamp recorded always, plus an optional one-click linkedFocusId, so resolving a focus can never bury a note. V1 targets the extension sidebar and the desktop companion.

asana.label: #222 Notes System — standalone notepad (sidebar + companion V1), optional focus linkage, Mimir opt-in sink

nodes.label: Test Suite
nodes.activity: 63 test files on Node's built-in node:test, plus chromeMock and supabaseFake fixtures. No React component tests, no E2E, no browser automation.
nodes.blurb: Strong where it counts and absent where it hurts. Pure helpers and service logic — sync resilience, attribution, outbox, sanitizers, schedule model, org permissions, migration lint — are well covered. UI verification is entirely manual, which is why the audits keep finding rendering-layer bugs (XSS sinks, blank preview panes, [object Object]) that no test could have caught.

nodes.label: Supabase Backend (project "Flux")
nodes.activity: 8/1: probed live — REST and auth endpoints both answer 401 'No API key found', i.e. the API is up and correctly rejecting unauthenticated calls. Controls example.com and supabase.com both 200.
nodes.blurb: The single spine every surface shares — and the hardest evidence that Tabatha is a Flux child rather than a sibling: the linked project is literally NAMED 'Flux' (ref mtdgoahskcibjbhfvofx). Postgres with a dedicated `tabatha` schema, Auth, Realtime, Storage, Edge Functions and pg_cron. One production project, no staging.

nodes.label: tabatha Schema (71 migrations)
nodes.activity: Migrations 001 → 060, with gaps at 029, 046-049 and 051-057 — the sequence jumps 045 → 050 → 058.
nodes.blurb: Roughly 40 tables and 34 SECURITY DEFINER functions covering focus items, checkpoints, events, clock sessions, desktop activity, calendars, orgs/teams, invites, devices, push and the Cortex ledger. Three migrations carry dedicated lint tests. The numbering gaps are worth noting: they mean migrations were drafted and abandoned, so the file list is not a reliable record of what was ever considered.

nodes.label: RLS & Manager Scoping
nodes.activity: 7/21: migration 015 fixed a recursion bug and 016 restored write RLS, but the revoke guard is still missing; 045 explicitly notes no policy change was made for its new columns.
nodes.blurb: Row-level security is what makes a single shared project safe for org/team scoping — and it is also the layer through which the XSS bug becomes cross-user. Migration 012's manager/team scoping means one user's focus label is readable in another user's browser, which is exactly why the unescaped-sinks bug was reclassified upward from self-XSS.

nodes.label: Edge Functions (11)
nodes.activity: Eleven deployed functions; three run on pg_cron (asana sync every 5 min, focus push every 1 min, schedule nudges every 5 min).
nodes.blurb: The server-side surface: asana-webhook, connect-asana, disconnect-asana, sync-asana-tasks, cortex-proxy, device-signout, feedback-to-asana, invite-check, pair-watch, send-focus-push, send-schedule-nudges. These are what let the watch and phone work without an extension anywhere near them.

nodes.label: pair-watch Function
nodes.activity: 7/25: Dex shipped a pair-watch fix plus brute-force hardening after the 2026-07-24 live E2E run.
nodes.blurb: Mints and redeems the 6-digit code that lets a watch join an account without ever seeing a password. Mint is JWT-authenticated; redeem is deliberately unauthenticated (verify_jwt=false) because the watch has no session yet — which is precisely why it needed brute-force hardening.

asana.label: [Dex] pair-watch fix + brute-force hardening — 2026-07-24

nodes.label: Web Push Functions
nodes.activity: send-focus-push covers timer_expired, drifted, checkpoint_stale and focus_away. send-schedule-nudges only does the clock-in nudge — its blockStart and idleNudge paths are marked v2/v3 and are NOT built.
nodes.blurb: VAPID Web Push driven by pg_cron, with dedup logging so a nudge cannot fire twice. This is the mechanism that makes the phone useful without the app open. Honest in its own header about what it does not yet do, which is more than most of this codebase's docs manage.

nodes.label: Sync Service (push)
nodes.activity: 7/25: sync forensics (Sable) and the sync-integrity cluster (Corin) both landed; two named root causes remain open.
nodes.blurb: 1206 lines of watermark-based push sync with a 20-row diagnostics ring and column-missing resilience. The architecture is deliberately asymmetric — mostly push-up, with only two narrow once-per-install pull-downs — which works until two devices disagree, and that disagreement is exactly Root Cause A.

asana.label: [Sable] Cross-surface sync forensics — 2026-07-24

nodes.label: Durable Cloud Outbox
nodes.activity: cloudWriteService is the single auth owner; page contexts enqueue into _cloudOutbox when the service worker is unreachable, flushed by an alarm.
nodes.blurb: The offline-and-flaky-worker safety net. Establishing 'background is the single auth owner' and routing every write through a durable queue is what stops MV3's service-worker lifecycle from silently eating user data — a real risk given the documented stale-worker failure mode.

nodes.label: Rehydrate & Bootstrap Pull
nodes.activity: Both run ONCE per install, gated by _dataRehydratedAt and _orgRegistryBootstrappedAt. desktop_activity rehydrate is explicitly 'intentionally NOT done here for day one'.
nodes.blurb: The only two paths that pull cloud state down into a fresh install — org registry bootstrap and a sign-in rehydrate of clock sessions, intent history and focus items. Because they are once-per-install, a device that drifts after that first pull has no repair path, which is the structural reason Root Cause A keeps producing symptoms.

nodes.label: Supabase Realtime
nodes.activity: Migrations 011/033/045 publish profiles, focus_items, browser_profile_status and browser_profiles to supabase_realtime. The Sidecar subscribes; the extension does NOT.
nodes.blurb: Live cross-surface updates — the reason a checkpoint on the watch appears on the phone within a second. The asymmetry matters: the phone is a realtime client and the browser extension is not, so the extension is always the last surface to learn that something changed.

nodes.label: Auth & Session Identity
nodes.activity: Web Locks disabled with a noop lock and a custom chrome.storage.local session adapter, so the service worker and every extension page share one session.
nodes.blurb: Getting Supabase auth to work inside MV3 took two dedicated fix PRs (#17, #18) to defeat a Web-Locks contention cascade. The result is solid, but the SMTP is still unbranded — sign-in mails come 'from supabase.co' because custom SMTP was never configured, blocked only on an app password.

gh.label: PR #17 — fix(auth): disable supabase-js Web Locks — fixes lock-contention abort cascade

nodes.label: Device Management
nodes.activity: Migration 045 added the device columns; 6.7.53/6.7.54 added session-aware revoked-row reclaim in application code. The RLS half is still missing.
nodes.blurb: A device roster with remote sign-out, built after ghost-stint chaos from installs that never died properly. The application-code fix works; the database does not enforce it, so the remote-sign-out guarantee is only as strong as the client honouring it. The audit also flags two non-cross-referencing 'your devices' systems (Devices panel vs Live Stints) as an overhaul theme.

edges.detail: Benign by design: a matching URL rule sets contextSource='url_rule' and the gate is skipped entirely. Severity low. First seen: Plan 038 (2026-07-20). This is the intended pressure valve, but it means a mis-scoped rule silently disables intentional friction for a whole domain with no user-visible signal that the gate was suppressed.

Four unescaped innerHTML sites in gatekeeper.js (:255,:265,:274,:297 — only :297 gets quote-only escaping). Severity HIGH. First seen: 2026-07-21 audit, re-verified worse than reported. Any focus label or inherited context containing markup renders as live HTML inside the gate. Workaround: none in place — no escapeHtml() helper exists anywhere in src/.

About 19 unescaped sites in inbar.js, including notes and descriptions rendered raw inside a <textarea> (:564,:601), the edit-dropdown focus list (:588→594), sticky-note pause text (:680/681), and nine auto-triggered overlay sites (:1258–:1608). Severity HIGH. First seen: 2026-07-21. Workaround: none. Fixing the textarea sinks needs care to preserve legitimate newlines.

The escalation path: migration 012's manager/team RLS scoping makes focus_items.label and checkpoint notes readable cross-user TODAY, so a malicious label written on one device renders unescaped in a manager's browser. Severity HIGH — this reclassifies the bug from self-XSS to genuine cross-user XSS. First seen: reclassified 2026-07-21. Workaround: none; RLS is working as designed, the sinks are the defect.

Break notes typed by the user are written to local React state only and silently discarded — the code comment says 'In production this would persist via sendMessage.' Severity MED, trust-critical: unlike its siblings this control is not badged 'SOON', so it presents as working. First seen: 2026-07-21 (Argus W1). Workaround: add the existing stub badge until real persistence lands.

Two broken paths on the most-used surface: clicking a focus in the edit dropdown sends only SWITCH_FOCUS and discards the typed name; pressing Save triggers autoQueueFromIntent, which severs the link just made and spawns a stray queued sub-focus. Severity MED-HIGH. First seen: root-caused 2026-07-25 (6.7.79). Workaround: none — fix shape and acceptance criteria are specced but unimplemented.

The stray sub-focus that B09 spawns is a real row in the focus tree, so the corruption outlives the InBar interaction and pollutes the queue and history. Severity MED. First seen: 2026-07-25. Workaround: manually resolve the orphan sub-focus.

A missed clock-in cannot be corrected at all: clockIn()/clockOut() take no arguments and hardcode new Date(), the handlers ignore any payload, and no EDIT_SHIFT handler exists. Severity HIGH for anyone billing against this data — the hours are simply lost. First seen: confirmed 2026-07-25 (#221). Workaround: none.

Work Shifts' '✏️ Edit Shift' renders as a disabled stub with a SOON badge, so the surface that should own shift correction advertises the capability without providing it. Severity MED. First seen: 2026-07-21. Workaround: none.

RESOLVED (6.7.71/6.7.73). While open, an active focus's elapsed time was undercounted by exactly its accumulated pause time on every surface except the extension, worsening with each pause/resume cycle. Severity was HIGH — it silently understated tracked work. First seen: reported by Malkio as 'syncing between surfaces still a little off'; fixed 2026-07-24 with a red-to-green unit test.

A revoked session's still-valid JWT can call the Supabase REST API directly, bypassing the extension UI, and clear its own revoked_at — defeating remote sign-out for that device. Scope is same-profile only, not arbitrary cross-user. Severity HIGH. First seen: 2026-07-21, re-confirmed still open after the 6.7.54 application-code fix. Workaround: the extension honours revocation; only a direct API caller can bypass it.

Migration 016 ships a bare USING/WITH CHECK on profile_id with no session-identity test, and migration 045 explicitly notes no policy change was made for its new device columns. Severity HIGH — the guarantee lives in application code only. First seen: 2026-07-21. Workaround: none; fix is a WITH CHECK clause or a BEFORE UPDATE trigger, sized S.

Cross-surface conflicts are arbitrated purely by recency, so the last writer wins regardless of whether it had current state. Severity HIGH — this is the architectural root beneath every 'sync is a little off' report. First seen: named in the 2026-07-24 sync forensics. Workaround: none; needs plan #047, which has a reserved number and no document.

Compounding factor: the only two cloud-to-local pulls run ONCE per install and are gated by stored timestamps, so a device that drifts after its first pull has no repair path and stays wrong indefinitely. Severity HIGH. First seen: 2026-07-24. Workaround: reinstall, which clears the gate flags.

Shift rows are keyed by an ID hashed from their own clock times, so clock adoption across devices inserts a duplicate shift instead of updating the existing one. Severity HIGH — it double-counts hours. First seen: named 2026-07-24/25. Workaround: manually delete duplicate shift rows.

Hard blocker on the clock-backdate feature: editing a shift time changes the hash the sync ID is derived from, so any edit would create a duplicate row rather than update one. Severity HIGH as a sequencing constraint. First seen: flagged inside the #221 spec itself. Workaround: land an immutable session id before building any time editing.

Benign, recorded for blast-radius honesty: the watch is a first-class checkpoint WRITER, so any change to checkpoint shape or the focus_checkpoints table breaks a surface that has no auto-update path and no release artifact. Severity LOW today, MED on schema change. First seen: watch 0.1.0 (2026-07-18). Workaround: treat checkpoint schema as a public contract.

RESOLVED in 0.2.1 (2026-07-23). While open, every repository call in SupabaseFocusRepository was unguarded, so any connectivity failure crashed the whole watch app — pause, resume, extend, resolve and checkpoint all took the process down. Severity was CRITICAL and it was named a ship-blocker for any watch release. Fixed by wrapping every call site in runCatching.

Assigning an OS window to an intent appears to work but never feeds time totals, so the companion records work that is silently discarded. Severity MED and trust-critical — a feature that looks like it tracks and does not is worse than an absent one. First seen: 2026-07-21. Workaround: none; deliberately escalated as a product-communication decision rather than silently patched.

Downstream consequence: desktop time assigned to an intent never reaches the hours that Work Shifts and Org Hours aggregate, so any total computed from companion assignments understates real work. Severity MED. First seen: 2026-07-21. Workaround: clock and focus through the extension or sidecar instead.

Supersession, not degradation: Tabby Sidecar took over the phone surface in July 2026 and both standalone mobile repos have been dead since 2026-05-30. Severity LOW as a defect, HIGH as a navigation hazard — two full repos with READMEs, plans and feature backlogs sit in the workspace looking live. First seen: divergence visible from the commit histograms. Workaround: archive both repos.

The version badge is hardcoded (v6.7.41) and eight shipped features are missing or stale across four pages — device management, extension-minted pairing codes, count direction/precision, un-resolve, phone-away heartbeat semantics, invites, TV sign-in and the PWA orientation fix. Severity MED. First seen: 2026-07-21. Workaround: none — and no freshness-check mechanism exists at all, so this recurs on every release.

The staff channel advertises 6.7.78 while the repo is at 6.7.82 — every staff install is four versions behind HEAD, including the 6.7.79-6.7.82 intake work. Severity MED. First seen: probed 2026-08-01. Workaround: run npm run publish:update; it is one command and fully automated.

The enterprise update.xml serves 6.7.78 to force-installed Workspace machines, so the managed fleet is also four versions behind. Severity MED. First seen: probed 2026-08-01. Workaround: the CRX pack-and-publish sequence in OPERATIONS.md §2.2b — manual, undocumented until archaeology found it, and unautomated in scripts/.

site/desktop/latest.json still points at desktop-v0.2.1 while desktop-v0.3.10 is the published release — the in-app updater will not offer eight patches' worth of fixes, including the 0.3.9 confirmation dialogs and the 0.3.10 update-check feedback. Severity MED-HIGH: users who need the update-visibility fix cannot receive it through the mechanism that fix repairs. First seen: 2026-08-01. Workaround: manual download from the GitHub release.

The newest store zip is 6.7.47, 35 versions behind HEAD, and the screenshots were generated from the showcase at roughly 6.7.18. Severity LOW while unpublished, but it becomes a launch blocker the moment the CWS item goes live. First seen: 2026-08-01. Workaround: rerun build:store and capture:showcase before submission.

Sequencing hazard: the audit is explicit that version and logo reconciliation must happen BEFORE any store submission, not after, and that the RLS revoke gap should close first too. Severity MED as a release-gate. First seen: 2026-07-21 (NOW #8). Workaround: sequence reconciliation ahead of submission.

Duplication hazard rather than a live failure: the widget writes public.flux_time_entries on its own Express server while the edge functions own the tabatha schema, so two independent Asana time paths exist with no reconciliation. Severity LOW while dormant, MED if it is ever restarted. First seen: superseded around 2026-07. Workaround: retire the widget or give it its own 0.x line as the system map recommends. Note it also commits TLS private keys into the tree.

Dependency gap: calendar is the last rung of #221's evidence ladder for proposing a missed clock-in time, but the Google OAuth sync engine was never built, so that rung is unavailable. Severity LOW — the higher-confidence rungs (companion OS activity, first focus, capture frame, tab activity) all exist. First seen: 2026-07-25. Workaround: rely on the earlier rungs.

Supersession: the Context View delivers the ambient focus-display job the Refocus screensaver was meant to do, on hardware the user already owns, which is why the screensaver went dormant at v2.0.0 with a local-only install. Severity LOW. First seen: Context View shipped 2026-07-18. Workaround: none needed — but ROADMAP.md Phase 5 still lists the screensaver integration as planned work, which is now misleading.

Forty concurrent worktrees all bump public/manifest.json on every commit (Headbox Rule 10), making it the repo's highest-contention shared file — a whole-file reformat would have forced a 98-line conflict onto 20 active branches, which is exactly why 6.7.82 exists as a revert. Severity MED as sustained friction. First seen: 2026-07-29. Workaround: keep the file at 2-space, the format the tooling already writes.

Root cause of the drift: with 40 worktrees each carrying its own version, 'current' is ambiguous by construction, and the single dist/ folder Chrome loads can be built from any of them. The July system map's top risk was that dist/ held 6.8.2 from an unmerged widget branch while Malkio believed he was running 6.7.22. Severity HIGH. First seen: 2026-07-19. Workaround: check git worktree list and each worktree's manifest before building, per the CLAUDE.md build/load constraint.

A dead worktree pointer left in the workspace root: its .git is a FILE whose target no longer resolves, so git commands there fail with 'not a repository (NULL)'. Severity LOW functionally, MED as a navigation trap — it looks like a live codebase with a full source tree and changelog. First seen: stale since 2026-05-18. Workaround: archive or delete the directory.

Documentation defect with real cost: the portfolio describes the Gatekeeper as a new-tab intercept, when the new tab is overridden by home.html and the Gatekeeper is an all-URLs document_start content script. Severity MED for anyone onboarding — it inverts the product's central mechanism. First seen: portfolio predates the 6.x line entirely. Workaround: read src/content/gatekeeper.js and public/manifest.json instead.

The portfolio lists 'Desktop Integration' as unstarted Phase 5 work and the workspace summary claims v0.1.0 shipped, while the companion is at 0.3.10 with 8703 lines of Rust and eleven published releases. Severity MED — it makes the most technically distinctive surface in the product invisible. First seen: 2026-08-01 cross-check. Workaround: read tabatha-desktop's git log and the GitHub release list.

ROADMAP.md Phase 5 lists 'Flux Master Interface' integration as future work, but the Supabase project Tabatha already runs on is literally named Flux and the Asana home is Flux Development. Severity LOW-MED: it frames the substrate as an aspiration, which misdirects planning about what integration work actually remains. First seen: 2026-08-01. Workaround: treat the Flux dependency as existing infrastructure.

Self-inflicted staleness: the internal system map is a point-in-time snapshot dated 2026-07-19 that is now wrong on nearly every specific (sidecar 0.2.1 vs 0.13.x, companion 0.2.1 vs 0.3.10, migrations 033 vs 060, extension 6.7.22 vs 6.7.82) while still reading as authoritative. Severity MED. First seen: 2026-08-01 cross-check. Workaround: regenerate it, or use this atlas.
